definition: Label propagation is a semi-supervised algorithm in machine learning that assigns labels to previously unlabeled data points.
details: At the start of the algorithm, a (generally small) subset of the data points have labels (or classifications). These labels are propagated to the unlabeled points throughout the course of the algorithm. Within complex networks, real networks tend to have community structure. Label propagation is an algorithm for finding communities. In comparison with other algorithms label propagation has advantages in its running time and amount of a priori information needed about the network structure (no parameter is required to be known beforehand). The disadvantage is that it produces no unique solution, but an aggregate of many solutions.

explainer.lead: Label propagation is a semi-supervised algorithm that assigns labels to unlabeled data points by spreading labels from a small labeled subset. In networks it is used for community detection, with advantages in running time and in needing little prior knowledge of network structure.

tiers.eli5: A few people in a crowd are told the answer, and they pass it along to their neighbors until almost everyone has heard it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it when labels are scarce, seeding a small labeled set and letting labels spread through the unlabeled points. In networks it finds communities without prior information about network structure.
tiers.paperLevel: Starting from a generally small labeled subset, labels are propagated to unlabeled points over the course of the algorithm. Compared with other community-detection algorithms it has advantages in running time and in the amount of a priori information required about network structure.

explainer.example: Given a social network where a few members are labeled as belonging to a community, label propagation spreads those labels to connected unlabeled members.
